title: Microfocused ultrasound plus a 1550 nm fractional laser versus ultrasound alone: split-face trial in 22 Asian patients
headline: Adding a 1550 nm non-ablative fractional laser to microfocused ultrasound improved wrinkles, dermal thickness and melanin index more than ultrasound alone over 24 weeks in 22 people with phototypes III to IV; deeper skin was not tested.
evidenceTier: RCT (split-face, evaluator-blinded), abstract read; full text not opened
fit: Device route: Weak for deep skin. Fractional lasers carry a higher pigment-change risk in deeper skin, and phototypes III to IV were the ceiling here.
regions: China (trial site); clinic procedure, availability varies by clinic
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Prices not looked up; cannot judge whether price tracks evidence.
summaryPoints: Observation (abstract read): 22 participants, 44 facial sides, two sessions six weeks apart, follow-up to 24 weeks. Both sides improved from baseline; the combination side improved more on wrinkle score, pigmentation index, dermal thickness, skin relaxation time and melanin index.
Observation: no difference between sides on a laxity scale or erythema index. Safety assessed by adverse events; details not in the abstract.
Inference: one laser added to a device is a procedure question; no conclusion for phototypes V and VI can be drawn.
Limits: n=22; Chinese cohort; abstract only; follow-up under 6 months.
fitLine: The result is probably real for the people studied, but it says nothing about the pigment-change risk I would want quantified for deeper skin.
timeline: Results at 24 weeks in the trial

fitAxes.why: Fractional laser aftercare needs strict sun protection; winter versus summer timing not addressed.
